name: diff
doc: The difference of two points, as a vector.
stmt: noncomputable def diff (p q : Pt n) : Pt n
proof: fun i => p i - q i

name: sqDist
doc:
**Squared distance** between two points: `Σᵢ (pᵢ - qᵢ)²`.

This is deliberately *not* `dist p q ^ 2`. It is the polynomial that the whole reduction works with,
and defining it directly means every lemma below is about a polynomial, not about a square of a square
root that happens to simplify.

It is exactly `sqNorm` applied to `diff p q`, which is why `sqNorm`'s two lemmas -- non-negativity and
"vanishes iff every component does" -- apply without restatement.
stmt: noncomputable def sqDist (p q : Pt n) : ℝ
proof: sqNorm (diff p q)

name: sqDist_eq_sqNorm
doc: `sqDist` is `sqNorm` of the difference. Stated so callers can rewrite rather than unfold.
stmt: theorem sqDist_eq_sqNorm (p q : Pt n) : sqDist p q = sqNorm (diff p q)
proof: rfl

name: sqDist_nonneg
doc: **Squared distance is non-negative.**
stmt: theorem sqDist_nonneg (p q : Pt n) : 0 ≤ sqDist p q
proof: sqNorm_nonneg _

name: sqDist_eq_zero_iff
doc:
**Squared distance vanishes exactly when the points coincide.**

The `←` direction is what makes the square layer replace `dist` faithfully: two points at distance
zero are the same point, so a constraint `sqDist a b = 0` is the constraint `a = b`.
stmt: theorem sqDist_eq_zero_iff (p q : Pt n) : sqDist p q = 0 ↔ p = q
proof:
by
  rw [sqDist]
  rw [sqNorm_eq_zero_iff]
  constructor
  · intro h
    funext i
    have := h i
    simp only [diff, Pi.sub_apply] at this
    linarith
  · intro h i
    rw [h]
    simp [diff]

name: dist
doc: **Distance**, the square root of `sqDist`. This is the only place a square root appears.
stmt: noncomputable def dist (p q : Pt n) : ℝ
proof: Real.sqrt (sqDist p q)

name: dist_nonneg
doc: Distance is non-negative, without any side condition.
stmt: theorem dist_nonneg (p q : Pt n) : 0 ≤ dist p q
proof: Real.sqrt_nonneg _

name: dist_sq
doc:
**Distance squared recovers the squared distance**, unconditionally.

`Real.sq_sqrt` needs non-negativity, which `sqDist_nonneg` supplies for free. This is why the square
layer costs nothing on the forward direction.
stmt: theorem dist_sq (p q : Pt n) : dist p q ^ 2 = sqDist p q
proof:
by
  rw [dist, Real.sq_sqrt (sqDist_nonneg p q)]

name: sqDist_eq_of_dist_eq
doc:
**Equal distances imply equal squared distances.**

This is the reduction: a `sqrt`-bearing constraint becomes a polynomial one, with no side condition.
The proof is `Real.sqrt_inj` after observing that both arguments are sums of squares -- the same three
steps `Lv-00` used at dimension two, now at every dimension.
stmt:
theorem sqDist_eq_of_dist_eq (p q r s : Pt n) (h : dist p q = dist r s) :
    sqDist p q = sqDist r s
proof:
by
  have h1 : 0 ≤ sqDist p q := sqDist_nonneg p q
  have h2 : 0 ≤ sqDist r s := sqDist_nonneg r s
  have h' : Real.sqrt (sqDist p q) = Real.sqrt (sqDist r s) := h
  exact (Real.sqrt_inj h1 h2).mp h'

name: dist_eq_of_sqDist_eq
doc:
**Equal squared distances imply equal distances**, given that one of them is the square of a
non-negative number.

The hypothesis `0 ≤ d` is not removable: `d` and `-d` have the same square, so without it the reverse
direction is false. Stating it here rather than in prose is the point of the whole `Geo` layer.
stmt:
theorem dist_eq_of_sqDist_eq (p q : Pt n) (d : ℝ) (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (h : sqDist p q = d ^ 2) : dist p q = d
proof:
by
  rw [dist, h]
  exact Real.sqrt_sq hd

name: sqDist_eq_of_dist_eq_same
doc:
**Equal distances to a common value imply equal squared distances.**

A specialisation of `sqDist_eq_of_dist_eq` that is the form constraints actually take:
`dist a b = d` and `dist c e = d` give `sqDist a b = sqDist c e` with no side condition.
stmt:
theorem sqDist_eq_of_dist_eq_same (p q r s : Pt n) (d : ℝ)
    (h₁ : dist p q = d) (h₂ : dist r s = d) : sqDist p q = sqDist r s
proof:
sqDist_eq_of_dist_eq p q r s (h₁.trans h₂.symm)

end Lattice.Geo

name: sqDist_eq_sum
doc:
**`sqDist` unfolded to a finite sum.** The form every continuity argument here consumes; the definition itself
goes through `sqNorm` and `diff`, which `simp` will not rewrite under an integral-like binder on its own.
stmt:
theorem sqDist_eq_sum (p q : Pt n) :
    sqDist (n := n) p q = ∑ i : Fin n, (p i - q i) ^ 2
proof:
by
  simp [sqDist, Lib.Linear.PenaltyVector.sqNorm, diff]

name: continuous_sqDist_right
doc:
**`sqDist p ·` is continuous in its second argument.**

A finite sum of squared coordinate differences: subtraction and squaring are continuous, and a finite sum of
continuous real-valued functions is continuous.
stmt:
theorem continuous_sqDist_right (p : Pt n) :
    Continuous (fun q : Pt n => sqDist (n := n) p q)
proof:
by
  simp only [sqDist, Lib.Linear.PenaltyVector.sqNorm, diff]
  continuity

end Lattice.Geo

name: coordDiff_sub_le
doc:
**两个点的差向量各分量之差 ≤ 2·rho。**

`(pts a i - pts b i) - (pts' a i - pts' b i) = (pts a i - pts' a i) - (pts b i - pts' b i)`，
两两对应相减。
proof:
by
  have h1 := abs_coord_sub_le_rho (n := n) (k := k) (pts := pts) (pts' := pts') (p := a) (i := i) ha
  have h2 := abs_coord_sub_le_rho (n := n) (k := k) (pts := pts) (pts' := pts') (p := b) (i := i) hb
  have heq : (pts a i - pts b i) - (pts' a i - pts' b i)
      = (pts a i - pts' a i) - (pts b i - pts' b i) := by ring
  rw [heq]
  calc |(pts a i - pts' a i) - (pts b i - pts' b i)|
      ≤ |pts a i - pts' a i| + |pts b i - pts' b i| := abs_sub _ _
    _ ≤ rho n k pts pts' + rho n k pts pts' := by linarith
    _ = 2 * rho n k pts pts' := by ring

name: coordDiff_add_le
doc:
**两个点的差向量各分量的和 ≤ 4·B。**

`|uᵢ + vᵢ| ≤ |uᵢ| + |vᵢ| ≤ 2B + 2B`，其中每个坐标 `|pts p i| ≤ B`。
proof:
by
  have h1 : |pts a i - pts b i| ≤ 2 * B := by
    have hx := hpts a i
    have hy := hpts b i
    calc |pts a i - pts b i| ≤ |pts a i| + |pts b i| := abs_sub _ _
      _ ≤ 2 * B := by linarith
  have h2 : |pts' a i - pts' b i| ≤ 2 * B := by
    have hx := hpts' a i
    have hy := hpts' b i
    calc |pts' a i - pts' b i| ≤ |pts' a i| + |pts' b i| := abs_sub _ _
      _ ≤ 2 * B := by linarith
  calc |(pts a i - pts b i) + (pts' a i - pts' b i)|
      ≤ |pts a i - pts b i| + |pts' a i - pts' b i| := abs_add _ _
    _ ≤ 2 * B + 2 * B := by linarith
    _ = 4 * B := by ring

name: sqDist_lipschitz
doc:
**`sqDist` 在 `rho` 下是 Lipschitz 的，常数 `8·n·B`。**

前提 `hpts`、`hpts'` 给出两组点各自的坐标界 `B ≥ 0`。**不可省**：
`sqDist` 涉及点的绝对位置，而 `rho` 只约束两条点列之间的差。

证明：逐项 `|uᵢ² - vᵢ²| = |uᵢ - vᵢ|·|uᵢ + vᵢ| ≤ 2ρ · 4B = 8Bρ`，`n` 项求和。
stmt:
theorem sqDist_lipschitz {n k : ℕ} {pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n} {a b : ℕ} {B : ℝ}
    (ha : a < k) (hb : b < k) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hpts : ∀ p i, |pts p i| ≤ B) (hpts' : ∀ p i, |pts' p i| ≤ B) :
    |sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) - sqDist (n := n) (pts' a) (pts' b)|
      ≤ (8 * n * B) * rho n k pts pts'
proof:
by
  have hρ := rho_nonneg n k pts pts'
                         
  have hterm : ∀ i : Fin n,
      |(pts a i - pts b i) ^ 2 - (pts' a i - pts' b i) ^ 2| ≤ (8 * B) * rho n k pts pts' := by
    intro i
    have hd := coordDiff_sub_le (n := n) (k := k) (pts := pts) (pts' := pts') (a := a) (b := b) ha hb i
    have hs := coordDiff_add_le (n := n) (pts := pts) (pts' := pts') (a := a) (b := b) hpts hpts' i
    have hfac : (pts a i - pts b i) ^ 2 - (pts' a i - pts' b i) ^ 2
        = ((pts a i - pts b i) - (pts' a i - pts' b i))
          * ((pts a i - pts b i) + (pts' a i - pts' b i)) := by ring
    rw [hfac, abs_mul]
    calc |(pts a i - pts b i) - (pts' a i - pts' b i)|
          * |(pts a i - pts b i) + (pts' a i - pts' b i)|
        ≤ (2 * rho n k pts pts') * (4 * B) :=
          mul_le_mul hd hs (abs_nonneg _) (by linarith [hρ])
      _ = (8 * B) * rho n k pts pts' := by ring
                
  unfold sqDist sqNorm diff
  rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  calc |∑ i : Fin n, ((pts a i - pts b i) ^ 2 - (pts' a i - pts' b i) ^ 2)|
      ≤ ∑ i : Fin n, |(pts a i - pts b i) ^ 2 - (pts' a i - pts' b i) ^ 2| :=
        Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ ≤ ∑ _i : Fin n, (8 * B) * rho n k pts pts' := Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => hterm i)
    _ = n * ((8 * B) * rho n k pts pts') := by simp
    _ = (8 * n * B) * rho n k pts pts' := by ring

end Lattice.Geo

name: GeoConstraintSet
doc:
**The symbolic engine's state**: a finite list of constraints.

A list rather than a set so that the engine's output is computable data, and duplicated entries are
harmless because entailment is idempotent.
stmt: abbrev GeoConstraintSet (n : ℕ) : Type
proof: List (GeoConstraint n)

name: ModelsGeo
doc: **A configuration satisfies a constraint set.**
stmt: noncomputable def ModelsGeo (G : GeoConstraintSet n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) : Prop
proof: ∀ c ∈ G, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts

name: EntailsGeo
doc:
**Entailment between constraint sets.**

`EntailsGeo G c` says every configuration that satisfies `G` also satisfies `c`. This is the predicate the
verification step asks about.
stmt: noncomputable def EntailsGeo (G : GeoConstraintSet n) (c : GeoConstraint n) : Prop
proof: ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n, ModelsGeo G pts → GeoConstraint.Holds c pts

name: entailsGeo_refl
doc: Entailment is reflexive in the strong sense: a constraint entails itself.
stmt: theorem entailsGeo_refl (c : GeoConstraint n) : EntailsGeo [c] c
proof:
by
  intro pts h
  exact h c (List.mem_singleton.mpr rfl)

name: entailsGeo_mono
doc: Monotonicity: adding constraints cannot destroy entailment.
stmt:
theorem entailsGeo_mono {G H : GeoConstraintSet n} {c : GeoConstraint n}
    (hsub : ∀ d ∈ G, d ∈ H) (h : EntailsGeo G c) : EntailsGeo H c
proof:
by
  intro pts hH
  exact h pts (fun d hd => hH d (hsub d hd))

name: Rule
doc:
**A sound inference rule.**

`sound` is the whole content: whatever makes the premises true makes the conclusion true. A rule cannot
be constructed without it, which is why the closure below is sound by construction rather than by
inspection.
stmt:
structure Rule (n : ℕ) where
                      
  prems : List (GeoConstraint n)
                        
  concl : GeoConstraint n
                                   
  sound : ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n,
    (∀ c ∈ prems, GeoConstraint.Holds c pts) → GeoConstraint.Holds concl pts

name: rule_entails
doc:
**Applying one rule**: if the closure so far entails every premise, it entails the conclusion.

This is where `Rule.sound` is consumed; it is a `Prop`-valued predicate rather than a list operation
because the engine's output should be justified, not merely computed.
stmt:
theorem rule_entails (r : Rule n) (G : GeoConstraintSet n)
    (h : ∀ c ∈ r.prems, EntailsGeo G c) : EntailsGeo G r.concl
proof:
by
  intro pts hG
  exact r.sound pts (fun c hc => h c hc pts hG)

name: Closed
doc:
**The engine's closure condition**: a constraint set is closed under a rule set when every rule whose
premises are already entailed has its conclusion entailed.
stmt: noncomputable def Closed (rules : List (Rule n)) (G : GeoConstraintSet n) : Prop
proof: ∀ r ∈ rules, (∀ c ∈ r.prems, EntailsGeo G c) → EntailsGeo G r.concl

name: step_sound
doc:
**One engine step is sound.**

If some rule in the engine has a conclusion `c` whose premises are all entailed by `G`, then `G` entails
`c`. This is the unit of engine correctness; multi-step inference is its transitive closure, and stating
it separately keeps each piece checkable.

`r ∈ rules` is `Prop`-valued on purpose: the engine is defined by what it *may* derive, and the
soundness statement quantifies over all legal derivations rather than over a particular evaluation
strategy.
stmt:
theorem step_sound (rules : List (Rule n)) (G : GeoConstraintSet n) (c : GeoConstraint n)
    (h : ∃ r ∈ rules, c = r.concl ∧ ∀ d ∈ r.prems, EntailsGeo G d) : EntailsGeo G c
proof:
by
  obtain ⟨r, _hr, hc, hpre⟩ := h
  subst hc
  exact rule_entails r G hpre

name: no_rules_no_steps
doc:
**The empty rule list derives nothing**, so the engine is not vacuous in one direction: with no rules
there is nothing to conclude. This is the base case that makes `step_sound` meaningful.
stmt:
theorem no_rules_no_steps (G : GeoConstraintSet n) (c : GeoConstraint n) :
    ¬ ∃ r ∈ ([] : List (Rule n)), c = r.concl ∧ ∀ d ∈ r.prems, EntailsGeo G d
proof:
by
  rintro ⟨r, hr, _⟩
  exact absurd hr (List.not_mem_nil r)

name: derivation_sound
doc:
**Every conclusion the engine can draw is entailed**, by transitivity of entailment along a derivation.

Stated as an induction on a derivation list: a derivation is a sequence of constraints, each of which is
either already in `G` or follows from earlier entries by a rule.
stmt:
theorem derivation_sound (rules : List (Rule n)) (G : GeoConstraintSet n)
    (steps : List (GeoConstraint n))
    (hstep : ∀ c ∈ steps,
      (c ∈ G) ∨ (∃ r ∈ rules, c = r.concl ∧ ∀ d ∈ r.prems, EntailsGeo G d)) :
    ∀ c ∈ steps, EntailsGeo G c
proof:
by
  intro c hc
  rcases hstep c hc with hin | hrule
  ·                                 
    intro pts hG
    exact hG c hin
  · exact step_sound rules G c hrule

end Lattice.Geo
